Subject: Quick follow-up + proposal for rotating demo slots

Hi Sophie / Liam,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the context on your real-time inference requirements and the throughput targets you mentioned (50–90 TPS peak with <150ms p95). As discussed, next step is a technical demo + capacity planning session where we can bring a solutions engineer and a runtime engineer.

To make scheduling simpler for your distributed team, a couple of proposals:
- Option A (rotating weekly): rotate meeting windows so the time moves between US-friendly / EU-friendly / APAC-friendly slots each week.
- Option B (fixed overlap): pick a fixed 90-minute overlap window that works for both EU and US, and invite APAC participants optionally via recording + follow-up deep-dive.

Can you share who needs to be on the demo from your side (SE/infra/procurement)? Also a quick check on timezone coverage: Sophie you are in Dublin (CEST), Liam in Boston (EDT) — is that still correct?

Below are three rotating-slot proposals for a recurring weekly 60-minute technical demo. Each bullet is listed as "US / EU / APAC" local times to make it easy to scan:

- Proposal 1 (even rotation, 60m)
  - Week 1: 09:00 PT / 17:00 BST / 00:00 SGT (next day)  
  - Week 2: 12:00 PT / 20:00 BST / 03:00 SGT  
  - Week 3: 15:00 PT / 23:00 BST / 06:00 SGT  

- Proposal 2 (US-friendly primary)
  - Week 1: 10:30 PT / 18:30 BST / 01:30 SGT
  - Week 2: 10:30 PT / 18:30 BST / 01:30 SGT
  - Week 3: 10:30 PT / 18:30 BST / 01:30 SGT

- Proposal 3 (short rotating windows + recordings)
  - 45m live with 15m async follow-up; rotate live time between US and EU every other week and always record for APAC.

I attached our product deck and a short demo brief with suggested agenda. If you like, I can send calendar invites for the first three rotating weeks using Proposal 1 so you can see how it lands.

Quick ask: which proposal do you prefer, and who from your team should be invited?

Thanks,
Marissa
